traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 209 Rutaceae: shrubs or trees, very rarely herbs (rue, Dictamnus); leaves simple or compound, mostly dotted with oil glands; no stipules; flowers rarely irregular; sepals 4 or 5, petals mostly free; stamens as many or twice as many as the petals; ovary superior, often of 4 or 5 joined carpels; fruit a berry (the citrus fruit among them), a drupe or a leathery fruit, rarely a capsule.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Rutaceae with Cneoraceae, Ptaeroxylaceae, Rhabdodendraceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 359, family Rutaceae: inflorescence cyme or raceme (rarely solitary), usually; read as {"cyme": "often", "raceme": "often"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 361, 362, family Rutaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite, usually; read as {"hermaphrodite": "usually"}.
